- If sentiment is consistently neutral or negative (0.00), model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope or add early mean-reversion term.
- When sentiment shows minor positive signals (e.g., 0.20–0.33), model overreacts; cap forecast growth to avoid over-optimism.
- If history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of decline), model should not assume continuation; adjust forecast toward historical mean.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture short-term volatility; add sentiment-weighted volatility buffer to forecast.
- If sentiment history includes multiple 0.00 entries followed by a spike, model tends to lag; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead to align with sentiment shift.
- When true outcome shows sharp downward correction after peak, model often fails to recognize it; add early warning signal if sentiment turns negative.
